methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops delivered by a Norfolk native directly combat the access gap through grassroots peer learning, creating distributed capability outside traditional tech hubs—a clear signal toward broad, community-driven fluency building.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's institutional partnership with AI Ready RVA consolidates AI education and innovation resources in Richmond's metro core, deepening regional capability but potentially reinforcing hub-and-spoke concentration rather than distributed access.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Opinion piece explicitly naming AI data centers as drivers of urban-rural divide signals that infrastructure concentration in NoVA is increasing geographic inequality without corresponding capability distribution to rural Virginia.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches online workforce training program - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's partnership with ed2go for on-demand workforce training suggests platform-mediated, shallow skill delivery reaching beyond metro areas—distributed access but through turnkey tools rather than deep capability building.

signals.title: Norfolk Southern deploys AI system to catch wheel defects before they break - The Business Journals
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk Southern's deployment of specialized AI for predictive maintenance demonstrates deep technical implementation in Hampton Roads' transportation sector, but signals concentration in established industrial players rather than broad workforce adoption.
